note: Reviewed specification of the root modules the app can install. build-components.sh builds each zip at the commit of its lock component, checks that every script in the zip is byte-identical to the module/ source at that commit, and writes assets/system-modules.json (this file plus digests). Requirements below come from each module's own customize.sh, update-binary and docs. lifecycle: destinations, start, stop, uninstall and recovery as the module's own scripts implement them. distribution: 'distributable' modules are built by default; 'internal' modules only with ZAIRENKAI_INTERNAL_BUILD=1, and the release gate refuses any catalog that contains one.

modules.name: Zairenkai System Module (Core)

magisk.evidence: Magisk docs/changes.md v21.2: 'Fix the magisk --install-module command'; the module's update-binary needs v20.4+

kernelsu.evidence: ksud cli.rs: module install|uninstall|list (tiann/KernelSU 6d31a61, KernelSU-Next b427a3f)

risks: zcored starts at boot from service.sh and restarts at most 5 times in 10 minutes.
Removing the module stops zcored, which restores any temporary override it made, and deletes /data/adb/zairenkai-core.

destinations.data: /data/adb/zairenkai-core (customize.sh creates it 0700; config.toml there is kept across installs)

lifecycle.startup: service.sh waits for sys.boot_completed, then runs bin/zcored run --dir /data/adb/zairenkai-core under a supervisor: exponential backoff, at most 5 starts in 10 minutes, then it stops and writes /data/adb/zairenkai-core/failed
lifecycle.shutdown: the supervisor stops when the manager's disable or remove marker exists; zcored restores temporary overrides on SIGTERM
lifecycle.uninstall: uninstall.sh sends SIGTERM to zcored, waits up to 30 s, then deletes /data/adb/zairenkai-core
lifecycle.recovery: disable or remove the module in the root manager (or its safe mode); /data/adb/zairenkai-core/failed and zcored.log record start failures
lifecycle.kernel: none beyond Android 10+ arm64 (customize.sh checks ARCH and API)
lifecycle.action: action.sh prints zcored ctl health (the manager's Action button)

modules.distribution_reason: Apache-2.0 (LICENSE and NOTICE at the pinned commit, inside the zip)

modules.name: Zairenkai-FAS

magisk.evidence: as zairenkai_core; FAS docs/CAPABILITIES.md: Magisk v20.4+

conflicts.reason: Another frame-aware scheduler writing the same cpufreq nodes (FAS docs/CAPABILITIES.md: running two FAS modules at once is not supported). Module id from shadow3aaa/fas-rs build.rs at 09ba876.

risks: While running, zfasd raises cpufreq scaling_min_freq floors within [cpuinfo_min, scaling_max] and restores them when it stops (FAS docs/CAPABILITIES.md).
Vendor performance agents may write the same nodes; FAS backs off on contention but does not disable them.

destinations.data: /data/adb/zairenkai-fas (customize.sh creates it 0700; config.toml there is kept)

lifecycle.startup: service.sh waits for sys.boot_completed plus 10 s, then supervises zfasd run --dir /data/adb/zairenkai-fas with exponential backoff; after every exit it runs zfasd restore so nothing stays boosted
lifecycle.shutdown: zfasd restores every cpufreq floor it raised when it stops (FAS docs/CAPABILITIES.md)
lifecycle.uninstall: uninstall.sh sends SIGTERM to zfasd, runs zfasd restore, and deletes /data/adb/zairenkai-fas only if the restore succeeded (otherwise it keeps restore.json and logs to /cache)
lifecycle.recovery: disable or remove the module in the root manager; zfasd restore restores recorded floors
lifecycle.action: action.sh shows zfasd status; KernelSU's WebUI serves webroot/

modules.distribution_reason: Zairenkai-FAS has no licence at the pinned commit; provenance audit in docs/integration/fas-provenance.md. Built only with ZAIRENKAI_INTERNAL_BUILD=1, for the maintainer's own development testing; never in a distributable build.
